question: What is the primary goal of Post-Abortion Care (PAC) services?

options.A: To diagnose and treat chronic pelvic inflammatory disease
options.B: To reduce maternal death and injury from unsafe abortions
options.C: To promote voluntary surgical sterilization for all women
options.D: To provide routine antenatal checkups for pregnant mothers

explanation: PAC is specifically structured as an emergency and follow-up response to lower the high rates of maternal mortality and morbidity linked to unsafe procedures. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h1)

question: Why is family planning counseling a must before a patient is discharged from PAC?

options.A: It helps prevent repeat unintended pregnancies and repeat abortions
options.B: It satisfies legal requirements for hospital record keeping
options.C: It determines the exact gestational age of the previous pregnancy
options.D: It completely eliminates the risk of postpartum depression

explanation: You'll learn in practice that fertility can return very quickly after an abortion. Giving contraceptive counseling right away empowers your patient to space or prevent future pregnancies safely. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h1)

question: Why do healthcare planners conduct a community needs assessment before setting up PAC services?

options.A: To recruit international doctors for specialized surgeries
options.B: To penalize traditional healers practicing in the village
options.C: To understand local barriers, health data, and access challenges
options.D: To determine the exact cost of medical equipment imports

explanation: A needs assessment helps us see what real-life factors delay care in the community—like transport issues or cultural fears—so we can design services that truly help people. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h2)

question: A clinic wants to start PAC services but faces frequent power cuts. What facility readiness step must come first?

options.A: Expanding the administrative office space for managers
options.B: Procuring a reliable backup generator or emergency lighting system
options.C: Printing new family planning brochures for the waiting room
options.D: Hiring a full-time accountant to manage patient billing

explanation: Emergency procedures need steady light and power! Having a backup power source is a top priority to keep patients safe during unexpected blackouts. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h2)

question: Which instrument is most commonly used for safe uterine evacuation during PAC procedures?
explanation: MVA kits use a gentle suction created by a handheld syringe to empty the uterus safely and effectively with minimal trauma to the patient. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h3)

question: Why is keeping a good stock of uterotonic drugs critical in a PAC unit?

options.A: To prevent or treat severe uterine bleeding and hemorrhage
options.B: To reverse the side effects of general anesthesia
options.C: To speed up the return of normal ovulation cycles
options.D: To relieve severe lower abdominal cramping pain

explanation: Uterotonics like oxytocin or misoprostol make the uterine muscle contract, which is a lifesaver for stopping dangerous blood loss after evacuation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h3)

question: Which of these is NOT an essential supply needed for comprehensive PAC services?
explanation: You'll find chemotherapy pumps in cancer care wards, not in standard Post-Abortion Care clinics! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of competency-based training over normal classroom lectures for PAC nurses?

options.A: It allows the training course to be completed in under one hour
options.B: It ensures learners prove practical clinical skill before treating patients
options.C: It focuses solely on reading policy documents and guidelines
options.D: It completely removes the need for any clinical supervisors

explanation: Competency-based learning is all about hands-on practice and actually mastering the skill, so you feel confident stepping into the clinical ward. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h4)

question: Why do clinical training programs for PAC providers include values clarification exercises?

options.A: To help staff recognize and manage personal biases that affect patient care
options.B: To improve the physical cleaning speed of surgical instruments
options.C: To train clinicians on repairing complex abdominal hernias
options.D: To teach nurses how to calculate hospital drug purchase budgets

explanation: As nurses, we learn to separate our personal beliefs from our professional duty, ensuring every patient gets respectful, non-judgmental emergency care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h4)

question: A patient arrives at the clinic pale, dizzy, with a fast pulse and severe tummy pain after an unsafe abortion. What is your immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Send the patient home with instructions to return next week
options.B: Begin lengthy administrative registration before any medical action
options.C: Wait for laboratory blood test results before providing any fluids
options.D: Stabilize vital signs, start IV fluids, and prepare for emergency care

explanation: Pale skin, rapid pulse, and dizziness are warning signs of shock and hemorrhage. Your quick action with IV fluids and stabilization can save a life! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h5)

question: When should a PAC clinic refer a patient to a higher-level surgical facility?

options.A: Whenever the client requests oral contraceptive pills for birth control
options.B: When the patient presents with signs of uterine perforation or severe bowel injury
options.C: As a routine step for every single woman who seeks post-abortion care
options.D: Only after the client has stayed in the clinic for two weeks

explanation: Complex emergencies like organ perforation go beyond basic primary clinics and need specialist surgical care to keep the patient safe. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h5)

question: Why is it so helpful to offer contraceptives right inside the PAC clinic before the patient leaves?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to talk about reproductive anatomy
options.B: It forces every client to accept an intrauterine device before leaving
options.C: It guarantees that the clinic receives extra financial donations
options.D: It removes the barrier of traveling elsewhere and ensures immediate protection

explanation: Providing birth control right on the spot ensures women leave fully protected before fertility returns, so they don't slip through the cracks of a separate referral. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h6)

question: How soon can a woman theoretically start ovulating again after experiencing an abortion?

options.B: Only after six full months have passed
options.C: Exactly one full year following treatment
options.D: As early as two weeks post-procedure

explanation: Fertility can bounce back remarkably fast after pregnancy termination, which is why birth control counseling must happen immediately during the PAC visit. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of tracking indicators in a PAC monitoring and evaluation system?

options.A: To publicly expose staff members who make clinical mistakes
options.B: To calculate individual nurses' salaries based on procedure counts
options.C: To reduce the total number of patients visiting the health facility
options.D: To measure service performance, track outcomes, and guide quality improvement

explanation: Monitoring and evaluation helps managers see what is working well and where gaps exist, so the facility can continuously improve patient care. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h7)

question: How do clinical audits and case reviews help improve healthcare delivery in a PAC unit?

options.A: By identifying system weaknesses and learning from them to prevent future errors
options.B: By creating strict rules that punish nurses for asking questions
options.C: By increasing the waiting time for patients arriving at the emergency room
options.D: By replacing all doctors and nurses with automated computer software

explanation: Good case reviews focus on fixing teamwork and hospital systems rather than pointing fingers, creating a much safer environment for both patients and staff. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T020#GNS226_U5_T020_h7)
